questions.stem: Why are steam burns more severe than burns from boiling water at the same temperature?

options.text: Steam is at a higher temperature than boiling water
Steam releases latent heat of vaporisation as it condenses on the skin, delivering much more energy
Steam moves faster than liquid water

questions.explanation: When steam at 100 degrees C condenses on skin, it releases a large amount of latent heat of vaporisation (2,260,000 J/kg for water) in addition to heat from cooling. Boiling water at 100 degrees C only transfers heat as it cools. The extra latent heat makes steam burns far more severe.
